discussion: A prolonged period of mostly Good to at worst low-end Moderate AQI air quality is expected into next week. Copious rain on Saturday should scour the atmosphere, resulting in Good air quality for all areas. Anything not scoured out by rain Saturday will be cleared by strong northwest winds on Sunday, keeping Good air quality in the forecast. Windy conditions continue Monday, with pristine air in place, resulting in persisting Good air quality. The regional airmass will be slow to degrade next week, allowing Good air quality to persist ahead of active weather into the middle to late part of the week. Fine particle concentrations will generally be highest in the pre-dawn hours through the morning rush hour, and lowest during the mid to late afternoon before sunset. For the latest air quality information, please visit our website here.  -MDE

The regional airmass will slowly degrade Tuesday and Wednesday as modestly lighter winds will allow mild accumulation of local pollutants. Still, the regional background remains very clean, which should keep the region within the Good air quality range both Tuesday and Wednesday. On Thursday, a strong surge of cold air accompanied by blustery conditions will also deliver a clean airmass, allowing Good air quality to persist across the region. For the latest air quality information, please visit our website here.  -MDE

Local emissions Wednesday will increase pollutant concentrations under a morning inversion. However, a couple hours after sunrise, the inversion will break and substantially clean air will exist across the region. The higher morning concentrations of fine particles will cause the daily average exposure to end up in the Moderate AQI range, even though specific afternoon conditions will largely be in the Good AQI range. On Thursday, a strong surge of cold air accompanied by blustery conditions will deliver a clean airmass, providing Good air quality across the region that will persist on Friday. For the latest air quality information, please visit our website here.  -MDE

A strong surge of cold air accompanied by blustery conditions Thursday will deliver a clean airmass, providing Good air quality across the region that will persist into Friday. On Saturday, southerly winds take over. This may cause an increase in regional fine particle concentrations, though sufficiently windy conditions Saturday should keep air quality in the Good range. A coastal storm system is possible on Sunday. The exact details and path of the storm significantly impact the air quality forecast. As of now, some snowfall is possible along and south of the I-95 corridor. Where snow is heavy, precipitation will scour the atmosphere. Where snow is lighter, snow will help to trap pollutants near the surface. That, along with ambiance wood burning over the weekend will promote air quality around the Good/Moderate AQI threshold due to fine particles. Behind the storm next week, blustery and cold conditions will foster Good air quality. For the latest air quality information, please visit our website here.  -MDE
